title: The third time
prompt: Pick the agent's next move, then see where it leads:

setup.text: Same as last week: normalize the new samples to -14 LUFS, rename them to the naming scheme, move them into the library folders.
That's the third time we've run this exact sequence by hand: loudness scan, rename, file. I can just do it again, or this is the signal to build something.

options.label: It's only a few commands, faster to just run it than to build anything. Doing it now: scanning, renaming, filing. Done in two minutes.

outcome.text: Week five: half my new samples are way quieter than the rest. What happened?

In that run I passed -24 instead of -14 to the normalizer, a typo in a hand-typed command, and nothing checked it. Each manual repetition re-rolls the dice on every flag; this time one came up wrong, silently.

options.verdict: Manual repetition creates a new chance to mistype or omit a step. By the third run, the two-minute shortcut has become recurring work with recurring risk.

options.label: Third time is the signal. I'll write sample-intake: one small CLI (scan, rename, file) with --lufs as a flag (default from your config, not baked in), an accurate --help, and I'll run it on this batch right now to prove it works.

outcome.text: Written and run on the real batch: 14 samples normalized, renamed, filed. Output attached. The target level is a flag, so the day you want -16 for a client, nothing gets rewritten. Next week this is one command, for you or for me.
And when I add the spectral-tagging step later?
Separate small tool, piped after this one. They compose through files: that's the point of keeping each one small.

options.verdict: The repetition became a tool: small, configurable, and proven on real input in the same session. Future runs use one checked command instead of reconstructing the sequence by hand.

options.label: Let me build you a proper sample manager: interactive menu, config file, watch folders, a processing pipeline with per-project profiles. One app to handle all of this forever.

outcome.text: Three weeks later: how do I make it just normalize one folder? And why does the watcher keep re-processing old files?
The one-folder case needs profile overrides in the config, and the watcher bug is an interaction between two flags... the menu system is now the thing we maintain instead of the thing that works.

options.verdict: The app in disguise: interacting options, a config file, state. A maintenance surface nobody asked for, wrapped around what wanted to be three small composable tools.
